title_tag: 7 Best Kayaking Tours in Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Clear kayaks with Burj Khalifa views, night paddles, the Palm and Hatta Dam day trips compared on price, age limits and pickup. Pick your paddle in 2 minutes.
h1_main: 7 Best Kayaking Experiences in Dubai in 2026
h1_muted: (Clear Kayaks, Night Paddles and Hatta Compared)
author_role: 7 kayak experiences compared on price, paddle time, location, age limits and pickup
lead: For most visitors the best kayaking in Dubai is the 1-hour clear kayak in Jumeirah at €32 per person: a see-through kayak on the lagoon by Jumeirah Bay Island with the Burj Khalifa on the skyline, and the most-reviewed option on this page. Want mountains instead of skyscrapers? The Hatta Dam day trip (€56) gives you an hour on the reservoir plus a full day of sightseeing, with pickup available.

Three things decide the booking. Age: every city night paddle and the clear kayak are 12+ only, so families with younger kids should look at the Palm (all ages), Hatta (kayak from 6) or the dolphin kayak at Atlantis (8+). Day or night: the illuminated night kayaks are priced per kayak for two, from €39 per person at Dubai Creek Harbour. Transport: only the two Hatta trips come with a driver; every city paddle is make-your-own-way.
Below are 7 kayak experiences, filterable by clear kayak, night paddle, skyline view, Hatta and kid-friendly, with what each price really buys.

items.title: Clear Kayaking Experience with Burj Khalifa View

review: This is the default kayak booking in Dubai for a reason. For €32 per person you get a full hour in a 100% transparent kayak on the calm lagoon between Jumeirah Bay Island and the skyline, with the Burj Khalifa on the horizon. No other daytime option on this page puts the clear hull and the skyline together at this price.

It is a self-guided paddle: an instructor briefs you on the equipment and safety, then you explore the lagoon at your own pace while the team stays nearby. Guests repeatedly mention staff taking photos and videos for them, which matters here because the photo is half of the appeal.

Two catches. Booking two people on one booking gets you a shared double kayak; if you each want your own, make separate bookings. And it is 12+ only, so families with younger children should look at Dukes The Palm or Hatta. The same operator runs the night version from the same base.

review: If you have a whole day, this is the most trip for the money on the page. From €56 per person you get a 9 to 10 hour guided day in Hatta: snacks in the village, 1 hour of kayaking on Hatta Dam between rocky mountains, Heritage Village, Hatta Hill Park, Al Khattem Dam and a photo stop at the Hatta sign, with an English and Arabic speaking guide throughout.

It is also the best pick for families with primary-school kids: the kayak minimum age is 6, against 12 for the city skyline paddles, and you can take a double kayak with a child. Paddlers with no experience get a water bicycle instead, which is worth knowing if anyone in your group has never held a paddle.

The catch is the fine print on what each option covers. The listing clearly includes pickup, the vehicle, snacks, water and the guide, and the kayak ticket on the private trip; for the shared and desert-combo options, check that the kayak ticket and lunch are in your price before you pay. If you want them guaranteed in writing, the Hatta kayak, hill walk and lunch tour spells both out.

review: The tighter, more active take on Hatta. €66 per person covers hotel pickup in an air-conditioned 4x4 (up to 6 guests per car), 1 hour of kayaking at Hatta Dam with the ticket included, a guided uphill walk at Hatta Hill Park to the panoramic viewpoint, a photo stop and a shawarma lunch with a cold drink.

Against the #2 Hatta sightseeing tour it costs about €10 more and lasts 7 hours instead of 9 to 10. You swap the Heritage Village, dams and reserve stops for more walking, and you get the kayak ticket and lunch written into the includes. That certainty is the main reason to pay the difference.

It is new, with 5 reviews, all 5 stars, so there is less track record than the other Hatta trip. Bring comfortable shoes, a sun hat, sunscreen, water and a change of clothes. Extra kayak time, quad biking and food beyond the included lunch are paid.

guide.h2: Which Kayak Tour Should You Book?
guide.html:
• One paddle, best value, skyline photo: the clear kayak with Burj Khalifa view at €32.
  • A free day and you want to leave the city: Hatta sightseeing with kayaking (€56), or the Hatta kayak, hill walk and lunch (€66) if you want pickup, kayak ticket and lunch all clearly included.
  • Night kayaking as a couple: the Jumeirah night kayak for the lit-up clear kayak, or the Creek Harbour neon kayak to save about €13 per kayak.
  • Kids under 12: Dukes The Palm (all ages), Hatta (kayak from 6) or the dolphin kayak (8+). Every city skyline paddle is 12+.
  • Stand-up paddleboarding: Dukes The Palm is the only option here with SUP.
  • Already planning a waterpark day: the dolphin kayak with Aquaventure pass.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Timing, What to Bring and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Day or night

The daytime clear kayak's listing tags it for sunrise and sunset, the softest light for the skyline photo. The two night paddles are lit kayaks priced per kayak for up to 2, so they are best value as a couple and expensive solo. Arrive 20 to 30 minutes early for the Jumeirah night kayak; at Creek Harbour there are no walk-ins and late arrivals are not compensated.

Age limits catch families out

The clear kayak and both night paddles are 12+ only. With younger children your options are Dukes The Palm (all ages), Hatta (kayak from 6, infants 0 to 3 free on a lap on the sightseeing tour) and the dolphin kayak at Atlantis (8+, with a paying adult paddling alongside under-12s).

What to bring

For every water option: a change of clothes. Bring swimwear for Dukes The Palm and Atlantis, and biodegradable sunscreen at Dukes. Shoes are not worn on the Jumeirah night kayaks, and sandals or flip-flops are not allowed on the clear kayak. For Hatta add comfortable walking shoes, a sun hat and water. At Atlantis bring a passport or ID card and leave cameras and jewellery behind.

Getting there and what costs extra

Only the two Hatta trips include transport; Hatta is about 1.5 hours each way by road. The city paddles in Jumeirah, the Palm and Creek Harbour are make-your-own-way. Watch for extras: on the #2 Hatta tour, check whether the kayak ticket and lunch are in your option; on the #5 Hatta tour, extra kayak time and quad biking are paid; at Atlantis the dolphin photos are not included.

Building a whole water day? Compare the best jet ski tours in Dubai for the same skyline at speed, or scuba diving in Dubai to go under the water instead of over it. For an evening in the dunes after a Hatta day, see our 10 desert safaris compared.

faqs.q: What is the best kayaking in Dubai?
faqs.a: For most visitors, the 1-hour clear kayak on the Jumeirah Bay lagoon at €32 per person: a transparent kayak with the Burj Khalifa on the skyline. For a full day out, the Hatta Dam kayaking tour from €56 adds mountains and sightseeing with pickup available.

faqs.q: How much does clear kayaking in Dubai cost?
faqs.a: The daytime clear kayak with Burj Khalifa views costs from €32 per person for 1 hour. The illuminated clear kayak at night costs €91 per kayak for up to 2 people, about €46 each.

faqs.q: Can you kayak at night in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. There are two night paddles: a lit-up transparent kayak on the Jumeirah Bay lagoon (€91 per kayak for 2) and a neon-lit kayak at Dubai Creek Harbour (€78 per kayak for 2). Both are 1 hour, guided, with Burj Khalifa views and for ages 12+.

faqs.q: Is Hatta kayaking worth the trip from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes if you have a full day: Hatta Dam sits among rocky mountains about 1.5 hours from Dubai, and the tours combine 1 hour of kayaking with sightseeing or a hill walk. The 7-hour tour at €66 includes hotel pickup, the kayak ticket and lunch.

faqs.q: Can children go kayaking in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, but check the age limit. The clear kayak and both night paddles are 12+. Dukes The Palm has no age limit listed, Hatta kayaking starts at 6, and the dolphin kayak at Atlantis is 8+ with a paying adult for under-12s.

No. The guided options start with a safety briefing, Dukes The Palm is set up for first-timers, and the night paddles are on calm water. On the Hatta sightseeing tour, guests with no experience use a water bicycle instead of a kayak.

faqs.q: Is there mangrove kayaking in this comparison?
faqs.a: No. None of the 7 bookable options compared here is a mangrove paddle; they cover the Jumeirah Bay lagoon, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Creek Harbour, Atlantis and Hatta Dam.

methodology: We compared 7 bookable kayak experiences in and around Dubai: the clear kayak and night kayak on the Jumeirah Bay lagoon, the Creek Harbour neon night paddle, kayak or SUP hire at Dukes The Palm, the dolphin kayak at Atlantis and two Hatta Dam day trips. Each was compared on price per person and per hour on the water, paddle time, location and view, day or night, kayak type, transport, age limits and what costs extra. Prices are live listing from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews.
